# Documentation for the DiagnostySize app

The DiagnostySize app is an application for calculating the sample size or the power in diagnostic accuracy studies.
The optimal calculation approach was developed by Stark et al.

First of all the user can select an endpoint.
If the user wants to calculate the *sample size* for a diagnostic accuracy trial, select *“sample size”*.
Alternatively, the user can calculate the *power* of a diagnostic accuracy study.
To do this, click on *“power”*.
Next, select a study design.
In the *single-arm trial*, each participant receives the experimental test and the reference standard test.

![Fig.1: Screenshot shows the endpoint and design choices](img/screenshot1.png)

The *comparative design* compares two tests.
One test is a previously evaluated comparator test and the second test is the experimental test.
When you select the *comparative design*, you can choose between two types of comparison design.
The *unpaired* approach and the *paired* approach.
In the *unpaired* approach, the participants are divided into two groups, one receiving the experimental test and the other receiving the comparator test.
Both groups also receive the reference standard test.\
In the *paired* design, each participant receives all three tests, the reference standard, the comparator and the experimental test.
In the comparative design, you can test whether the experimental test is *superior* to the comparative test, or you can set a *non-inferiority* boundary for both endpoints (sensitivity and specificity).

![Fig.2: Screenshot shows the non-inferiority limits and a tooltip with additional informations](img/screenshot3.png)

If the user chooses a non-inferiority boundary, the alpha value entered is divided by 2 because alpha is one-sided in a non-inferiority test.

Once these choices have been made, the user must complete the form displayed.
There are default values that can be easily replaced or adjusted.
The arrows on the right of the input box allow the user to move up and down by 0.01 steps.

![Fig.3: Screenshot shows the numeric input field with arrow to change the value.](img/screenshot2.png)

Note: The values are processed using a decimal point as the decimal separator. If the browser language is set to German, the separator may be displayed as a comma instead.

Valid entries are between 0 and 1 in each field, except for the sample size, which is valid between 0 and 999999. Leaving an input field empty causes errors. Pleas fill out all of the input fields.
If a negative value is entered, an error message is displayed in the main part of the application.\
For further information, the user can hover over the input field and an additional explanation of the value will pop up.
An example of this additional information is shown in screenshot 2 & 3.
In screenshot 1 you can see question mark button which, when clicked, displays further explanations about the study designs.

The right hand side of the application displays the results of the calculation.
These change as the design or input values are changed.
Below the calculation results is a result text listing the input and output values.
Also there is information about the paper published by Stark et al.
These papers serve as the basis for the sample size or power calculation .

# Notation

-   $N_{se}$ : Total sample size to reject the null hypothesis regarding sensitivity

-   $N_{sp}$ : Total sample size to reject the null hypothesis regarding specificity

-   $n_{se}$ : The minimum number of subjects with the targeted condition to reject the null hypothesis regarding sensitivity

-   $n_{sp}$ : The minimum number of healthy participants to reject the null hypothesis regarding specificity

-   $\pi$ : Prevalence

-   $\alpha$ : Significance level (two-sided alpha)

-   $Se_0$ : The minimum sensitivity threshold (single-arm trial)

-   $Sp_0$ : The minimum specificity threshold (single-arm trial)

-   $Se_E, Sp_E$ : The values of sensitivity and specificity of the experimental test

-   $Se_C, Sp_C$ : The values of sensitivity and specificity of the comparative test

-   $V(Se), V(Sp)$ : The variance of the parameters sensitivity and specificity

-   $z_{\alpha/2}$ and $z_{\beta}$ : The quantile of the standard normal distribution

-   $Power_t$ : The overall power

-   $Power_{se}$ and $Power_{sp}$ : The power to show the sensitivity and power the specificity
-  $H_{0_{global}}$ is the global null hypothesis and can only be rejected if both hypothesis $H_{0_{Se}}$ and $H_{0_{Sp}}$ are rejected. This applies to all of the following hypothesis.

# Equations

| Endpoint| Design | Hypothesis | Equations |
|----------|-------------|:----------------|:-----------------------------------|
| sample size | single arm |$$H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_0 \\ H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_0 $$  | \\[ N_{Se}= \frac{[z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{V(Se_0)}+ z_{\beta{se}}\sqrt{V(Se_E)}]^2}{(Se_0-Se_E)^2\cdot\pi} \\\\N_{Sp}=\frac{[z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{V(Sp_0)}+z_{\beta_{sp}}\sqrt{V(Sp_0)}]^2}{(Sp_0-Sp_E)^2\cdot(1-\pi)}\\] |
| sample size | comparative unpaired superiority |\\[H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C\\] | \\[ N_{Se}=\frac{(z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{V_0(Se_C-Se_E)}+z_{\beta_{se}}\sqrt{V_A(Se_C-Se_E)})^2}{(Se_C-Se_E)^2\cdot\pi} \\\\N_{Sp}=\frac{(z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{V_0(Sp_C-Sp_E)}+z_{\frac{1-\beta_{se}-Power_t}{1-\beta_{se}} }\sqrt{V_A(Sp_C-Sp_E)})^2}{(Sp_C-Sp_E)^2\cdot(1-\pi)} \\] |
| sample size |comparative paired superiority |\\[H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C\\] | \\[N_{Se}= \frac{(z_{1-\alpha/2}\cdot\psi_D+z_{1-\beta_{se}}\sqrt{\psi_D^2-\frac{1}{4}(Se_C-Se_E)^2(3+\psi_D)})^2}{\psi_D(Se_C-Se_E)^2\pi} \\\\N_{Sp}= \frac{(z_{1-\alpha/2}\cdot\psi_{ND}+z_{\frac{Power_t}{1-\beta_{se}}}\sqrt{\psi_{ND}^2-\frac{1}{4}(Sp_C-Sp_E)^2(3+\psi_{ND})})^2}{\psi_{ND}(Sp_C-Sp_E)^2(1-\pi)} \\] |
| sample size |comparative unpaired non-inferiority |\\[H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C - \Delta_{Se} \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C -\Delta\_{Sp}\\] | \\[N_{Se}= \frac{(z_{\alpha/2}+z_{\beta_{Se}})^2\cdot V_A(Se_C-Se_E)}{(Se_C-Se_E-\Delta_{Se})^2\cdot\pi}\\\\N_{Sp}= \frac{(z_{\alpha/2}+z_{\beta_{\frac{1-\beta_{Se}-Power_t}{1-\beta_{Se}}}})^2\cdot V_A(Sp_C-Sp_E)}{(Sp_C-Sp_E-\Delta_{Sp})^2\cdot(1-\pi)} \\] |
| sample size | comparative paired non-inferiority |\\[H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C - \Delta_{Se} \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C -\Delta\_{Sp}\\] | \\[ N_{Se}=\frac{(\psi_D-(Se_E -Se_C)^2)(\frac{z_{\alpha/2}}{w_{u_{Se}}}+z_{\beta_{Se}})^2}{(-\Delta_{Se}-(Se_E-Se_C))^2\cdot \pi} \\\\ N_{Sp}=\frac{(\psi_{ND}-(Sp_E -Sp_C)^2)(\frac{z_{\alpha/2}}{w_{u_{Sp}}}+z_{\frac{1-\beta_{Se}-Power_t}{1-\beta_{Se}}})^2}{(-\Delta_{Sp}-(Sp_E-Sp_C))^2\cdot (1-\pi)} \\] |
| sample size | comparative unpaired se sup sp non-inf |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C - \Delta_{Sp} \\] | \\[  N_{Se}=\frac{z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}\sqrt{V_0(Se_C-Se_E)}+z_{\beta_{se}}\sqrt{V_A(Se_C-Se_E)}^2}{(Se_C-Se_E)^2\cdot\pi}\\\\ N_{Sp}=\frac{(z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}+z_{\beta_{\frac{1-\beta_{Se}-Power_t}{1-\beta_{Se}}}})^2\cdot V_A(Sp_C-Sp_E)}{(Sp_C-Sp_E-\Delta_{Sp})^2\cdot(1-\pi)} \\] |
| sample size | comparative unpaired sp sup se non-inf |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C - \Delta_{Se} \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C  \\]  | \\[ N_{Se}=\frac{(z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}+z_{\beta_{Se}})^2\cdot V_A(Se_C-Se_E)}{(Se_C-Se_E-\Delta_{Se})^2\cdot \pi} \\\\ N_{Sp}=\frac{(z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}\sqrt{V_0(Sp_C-Sp_E)}+z_{\frac{1-\beta_{se}-Power_t}{1-\beta_{se}}}\sqrt{V_A(Sp_C-Sp_E)})^2}{(Sp_C-Sp_E)^2\cdot(1-\pi)}  \\] |
| sample size |comparative paired se sup sp non-inf |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C - \Delta_{Sp} \\] | \\[ N_{Se}=\frac{(z_{1-\frac{\alpha}{2}}\cdot\psi_D + z_{1-\beta_{se}}\sqrt{\psi_D^2-\frac{1}{4}(Se_C-Se_E)^2(3+\psi_D)})^2}{\psi_D(Se_C-Se_E)^2\cdot\pi}\\\\ N_{Sp}=\frac{(\psi_{ND}-(Sp_E -Sp_C)^2)(\frac{z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{w_{u_{Sp}}}+z_{\frac{1-\beta_{Se}-Power_t}{1-\beta_{Se}}})^2}{(-\Delta_{Sp}-(Sp_E-Sp_C))^2\cdot (1-\pi)} \\] |
| sample size | comparative paired sp sup se non-inf |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C - \Delta_{Se} \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C  \\] | \\[  N_{Se}= \frac{(\psi_D-(Se_E -Se_C)^2)(\frac{z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{w_{u_{Se}}}+z_{\beta_{Se}})^2}{(-\Delta_{Se}-(Se_E-Se_C))^2\cdot \pi}\\\\ N_{Sp}=\frac{(z_{1-\frac{\alpha}{2}}\cdot\psi_{ND}+z_{\frac{Power_t}{1-\beta_{se}}}{\sqrt{\psi_{ND}^2-\frac{1}{4}(Sp_C-Sp_E)^2(3+\psi_{ND})}})^2}{\psi_{ND}(Sp_C-Sp_E)^2(1-\pi)}   \\] |
| Power | single arm  |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_0 \leq Se_E\\\\ H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_0\leq Sp_E \\]  | \\[  Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{se}}= \frac{n_{se}\cdot(Se_0-Se_E)^2-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}\sqrt{V(Se_0)}}{\sqrt{V(Se_E)}^2}\\\\ Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{sp}}= \frac{n_{sp}\cdot(Sp_0-Sp_E)^2-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}\sqrt{V(Sp_0)}}{\sqrt{V(Sp_E)}^2}\\] |
| Power | comparative unpaired superiority | \\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C \\] | \\[ Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{se}} = \frac{n_{se}\cdot(Se_C-Se_E)^2-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}\sqrt{V_0(Se_C-Se_E)}}{\sqrt{V_A(Se_C-Se_E)}^2}\\\\Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{sp}} = \frac{n_{sp}\cdot(Sp_C-Sp_E)^2-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}\sqrt{V_0(Sp_C-Sp_E)}}{\sqrt{V_A(Sp_C-Sp_E)}^2}\\] |
| Power | comparative paired superiority |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C  \\]  |\\[   Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\ z_{1-\beta_{se}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{se}}\cdot\sqrt{\psi_D}(Se_C-Se_E)-z_{1-\frac{\alpha}{2}}\cdot\psi_D}{\sqrt{\psi_D^2-\frac{1}{4}(Se_c-Se_E)^2(3+\psi_D)}}\\\\Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\z_{1-\beta_{sp}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{sp}}\cdot\sqrt{\psi_{ND}}(Sp_C-Sp_E)-z_{1-\frac{\alpha}{2}}\cdot\psi_{ND}}{\sqrt{\psi_{ND}^2-\frac{1}{4}(Sp_c-Sp_E)^2(3+\psi_{ND})}}\\]  |
| Power | comparative unpaired non-inferiority |\\[H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C - \Delta_{Se} \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C -\Delta\_{Sp}\\]  |\\[Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\z_{\beta_{se}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{se}}\cdot(Se_C-Se_E-\Delta)-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{\sqrt{V_A(Se_C-Se_E}}\\\\ Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{sp}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{sp}}\cdot(Sp_C-Sp_E-\Delta)-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{\sqrt{V_A(Sp_C-Sp_E}} \\] |
| Power | comparative paired non-inferiority | \\[H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C - \Delta_{Se} \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C -\Delta\_{Sp}\\] |\\[ Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{se}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{se}}\cdot(-\Delta_{Se}-(Se_E-Se_C))-\frac{z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{Wu_{Se}}}{(\sqrt{\psi_D}-(Se_E-Se_C))}\\\\Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{sp}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{sp}}\cdot(-\Delta_{Sp}-(Sp_E-Sp_C))-\frac{z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{Wu_{Sp}}}{(\sqrt{\psi_{ND}}-(Sp_E-Sp_C))}\\] |
| Power | comparative unpaired se sup sp non-inf |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C - \Delta_{Sp} \\] | \\[  Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{se}} = \frac{n_{se}\cdot(Se_C-Se_E)^2-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}\sqrt{V_0(Se_C-Se_E)}}{\sqrt{V_A(Se_C-Se_E)}^2}\\\\ Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{sp}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{sp}}\cdot(Sp_C-Sp_E-\Delta)-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{\sqrt{V_A(Sp_C-Sp_E}}\\]|
| Power | comparative unpaired sp sup se non-inf |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C - \Delta_{Se} \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C  \\]  |\\[ Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\ z_{\beta_{se}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{se}}\cdot(Se_C-Se_E-\Delta)-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{\sqrt{V_A(Se_C-Se_E}}\\\\ Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\z_{\beta_{sp}} = \frac{n_{sp}\cdot(Sp_C-Sp_E)^2-z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}\sqrt{V_0(Sp_C-Sp_E)}}{\sqrt{V_A(Sp_C-Sp_E)}^2}\\] |
| Power | comparative paired se sup sp non-inf | \\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C - \Delta_{Sp} \\] |\\[ Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\ z_{1-\beta_{se}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{se}}\cdot\sqrt{\psi_D}(Se_C-Se_E)-z_{1-\frac{\alpha}{2}}\cdot\psi_D}{\sqrt{\psi_D^2-\frac{1}{4}(Se_c-Se_E)^2(3+\psi_D)}}\\\\ Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\z_{\beta_{sp}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{sp}}\cdot(-\Delta_{Sp}-(Sp_E-Sp_C))-\frac{z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{Wu_{Sp}}}{(\sqrt{\psi_{ND}}-(Sp_E-Sp_C))}\\] |
| Power | comparative paired sp sup se non-inf |\\[ H_{0_{Se}}: Se_E \leq Se_C - \Delta_{Se} \\\\H_{0_{Sp}}: Sp_E \leq Sp_C  \\] |\\[ Power_{Se}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{se}})\\\\z_{\beta_{se}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{se}}\cdot(-\Delta_{Se}-(Se_E-Se_C))-\frac{z_{\frac{\alpha}{2}}}{Wu_{Se}}}{(\sqrt{\psi_D}-(Se_E-Se_C))}\\\\Power_{Sp}= 1-\Phi(z_{\beta_{sp}})\\\\z_{1-\beta_{sp}} = \frac{\sqrt{n_{sp}}\cdot\sqrt{\psi_{ND}}(Sp_C-Sp_E)-z_{1-\frac{\alpha}{2}}\cdot\psi_{ND}}{\sqrt{\psi_{ND}^2-\frac{1}{4}(Sp_c-Sp_E)^2(3+\psi_{ND})}}\\] |
